narrative.text: Vyktor Reznik is standing by the window, which is unusual — Vyktor does not stand when he can sit, does not look at views when he can look at documents. Lucen, his junior aide, is by the door. They stop talking the moment you enter. That pause. The one that means the conversation was about you and they are deciding whether to continue it in your presence. The pause is information.
There is something you need to know before this meeting.

Lucen is looking at the floor. Not with guilt — with the specific discomfort of a junior staffer who has learned something that is above his clearance. Vyktor waits. He wants you to ask. Or he wants you to already know.
Vael made a separate offer. To someone else in this government.
A beat. A long one. You can feel the weight of the next sentence before he says it.
